_comment: Canonical pack-store catalogue for Defenders of the Realm. Packs 1-5 (tiers 1-5) are the original pricing-ladder packs extracted VERBATIM from docs/monetization-v2-spec.md §4/§5/§8.4 — names are canon, never paraphrase. Packs 6-13 (tiers 6-13) are the STARTER STORE BUNDLES authored 2026-06-28 (WorkOrders/WORK_ORDER_store_packs_content.md) per the monetization audit (docs/audits/AUDIT_monetization_2026-06-28.md) to give the PackStore a full, compelling launch shelf. Each bundle is themed and price-anchored to an existing ladder point ($4.99/$9.99/$19.99); tier is a UNIQUE lookup key (PackCatalog.FindByTier), not the price. Every referenced cosmetic SKU has a matching entry in cosmetics.json so no granted cosmetic is dangling.

_schemaNotes.packDef: Each entry mirrors React's PackDef: sku, tier, name, tagline, pricing { usd, usdc, sol, skr }, contents { cosmetics, economy, convenience }, founderOnly?, packExclusiveCosmetic. The Unity loader deserializes each entry straight into a PackDef record.
_schemaNotes.pricing: usd is the Stripe/USD reference price; usdc/sol/skr are the per-currency wallet-rail amounts. The Unity wallet module reads sol/usdc/skr only. Starter bundles reuse the three ladder price points: $4.99 -> {usdc 4.99, sol 0.045, skr 60}; $9.99 -> {usdc 9.99, sol 0.09, skr 120}; $19.99 -> {usdc 19.99, sol 0.18, skr 240}.
_schemaNotes.tier: Unique 1..N lookup key (PackCatalog.FindByTier). NOT the price band — multiple bundles share a price point but each has a unique tier.
_schemaNotes.convenience: TIME-SAVING only, never combat-power (the bent covenant, §5.3). instant-build / instant-repair / harvest-auto-collect / xp-weekend / lantern-oil-2x-expedition / lantern-oil-3x-expedition. Lantern blessings are consumed per expedition. No permanent passives.
_schemaNotes.economy: In-game currency top-ups (§5.2). GameState applies crystals/food/coins; glimmer is carried for catalogue completeness (not yet applied at runtime per the audit).
_schemaNotes.impulsePacks: Packs 14-25 (tiers 14-25) are the WO-1037 SINGLE-RESOURCE IMPULSE PACKS, authored 2026-08-17 under the owner ruling of 2026-08-16 (option (b), verbatim: "we should have small instant packs" / "small wood only") and legalised by the WO-947 s12 amendment (the PURCHASE boundary is not the COST boundary). ONE family per harvestable resource (wood, iron, food, crystals) x small/medium/large. THE LOAD-BEARING RULE: each of these SKUs carries EXACTLY ONE economy key and an EMPTY cosmetics + convenience list. A multi-resource impulse bundle would re-mix the WO-947 cost baskets through the back door and is FORBIDDEN (WO-947 s12c guardrail 1) - asserted headlessly by DeNelle.Editor.Regression.ImpulsePackRegression [impulse-pack], which also pins the $5 PRICE CEILING (owner standing ruling, memory solana-store-early-access-pack-pricing) and the no-structures/no-levels/no-queue-completions rule. AMOUNTS ARE PENDING OWNER RATIFICATION - they were sized against the REAL demand curve read out of building-tiers.json (tier costWood 500..16000, costFood 300..13000, costCrystal 100..4800) and structures-catalog.json (repo.upgradeCost iron 20..1440): small closes the cheapest tier upgrade (the Lumber Mill T1 900-wood shortfall in the screenshot that prompted this WO), medium closes a mid-ladder step, large closes a late step but deliberately NOT the Barracks T6 16000-wood ceiling, so the top pack does not trivialise the game. The optional impulse/impulseResource/impulseSize fields are the machine-readable family tag ShortfallPackOffer resolves on; older packs omit them (absent = false/null, no migration break).
_schemaNotes.cosmeticGrant: Every cosmetics[] SKU is recorded into OwnedItemIds on grant and MUST exist in cosmetics.json (id == the SKU) or it is unredeemable. Starter-bundle cosmetics live in cosmetics.json with unlockMethod 'achievement' + glimmerCost 0 (owned via entitlement, equippable, not glimmer-buyable).

currencyDisclaimer: Token price moves with the market.
